analysis: The only change in ProviderLoop.swift is head lines 787-796, which add stored state to the ProviderLoop actor: coordinatorConnection (DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection?), unauthorizedSince, lastUnauthorizedReconnectAt, unauthorizedReconnectAttempts, and unauthorizedReconnectJitter (random in 0..<UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.thresholdJitter). These are internal, in-memory variables with no logic in this file. They do not touch authorization grants, attestation verification, encryption or key handling, prefix-cache storage, or the wire protocol, so no trust boundary behavior changes here. The comments reference a companion file, ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery, which is not in the supplied evidence. That file would hold the logic that reads these variables to trigger a reconnect when the coordinator marks the connection not routable, and it likely reads or writes the daemon state file. Open questions for integration: (1) whether the recovery reconnect is bounded and backed off, using unauthorizedReconnectAttempts and the jitter, so a hostile or flapping coordinator verdict cannot cause a reconnect storm (T-057, availability); (2) whether reconnecting preserves the T-053 binding of authorization to a connection, endpoint and generation, and never reuses stale grants; (3) whether coordinatorConnection published to the daemon state file leaks identifiers (T-058, evidence/diagnostics leakage). Because the logic is unseen, none of these can be judged from this unit. I identified no regression or finding in the visible changes. needs_deeper_review is set true only because the companion recovery logic and the DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection definition were not supplied.
